validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/SPEC: confirmed via 2 independent trade/primary sources that do NOT trace to GEM. NS Energy Business's Zohr project profile states verbatim: 'gas produced by the field is transported through two 216km-long and 30in-diameter pipelines connecting to an onshore gas treatment facility at El-Gamil.' Eni's own Aug-2019 press release ('Zohr gas production reaches 2.7 bcfd') independently corroborates the same twin-pipeline system and states the SECOND of the two lines - explicitly '216 km long 30" pipeline' - started up on 18 August 2019. GEM's P5132 (len=216.00 km, dia=30 in, StartYear1=2019, Shorouk concession->Al Gamil/Port Said, Fuel=Gas, FuelSource=Zohr Field, PipelineType=transmission) matches this SECOND pipeline's specs exactly (216 km/30in/2019), not the first (which came online with first gas in Dec 2017). This is correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk (offshore subsea gathering line from wellhead platforms to an onshore treatment plant), not a plant-internal or oil/NGL line. CAVEAT 1 (labeling, not a data error): this row's internal segment label 'Pipeline 1' is misleading given the evidence - the specs (216km, 2019 start) match the chronologically SECOND pipeline of the pair, while the sibling ProjectID P6036 (same pipeline name, len=210 km, same route) is presumably the first (op. since Dec 2017); worth a human check that segment ordering/labels aren't swapped, though the two rows are correctly kept as two separate physical pipes (not a duplicate - Eni/NS Energy both confirm TWO real, parallel 216km/30in lines exist). CAVEAT 2 (minor spec note, on the sibling not this row): P6036 carries len=210 km vs the 216 km both sources give for BOTH pipelines - a small discrepancy worth flagging to whoever researches P6036, out of scope here. CAVEAT 3: the current Status/PipelineType/Diameter ref (nsenergybusiness ...?cf-view) verifies OK for PipelineType and Diameter content but the literal word 'operating' is not present on the page for the Status value-check - the page still supports 'operating' by strong implication (production ramp-up narrative, ongoing since 2017-2019) and is corroborated by Eni's own release; tier medium-high for Status specifically, high for Length/Diameter/Fuel/FuelSource/PipelineType/StartYear.

validity.researcher_notes: The Owner fields currently on this row (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co 48%, Eni SpA 26%, Naturgy 13%, SEGAS 13%) do not match any sourced ownership structure for the Zohr subsea pipeline or the Shorouk concession it serves. Independent sources: Mubadala's own 2018 press release on completing its Shorouk-concession stake acquisition states plainly 'Eni, through its subsidiary IEOC, holds a 50 percent interest in the concession. The other partners in the concession are BP with 10 percent interest and Rosneft with 30 percent interest' (+ Mubadala's 10%) - i.e. Eni/IEOC 50%, Rosneft 30%, BP 10%, Mubadala Petroleum 10%, operated by Petrobel on behalf of PetroShorouk (the concession JV that also includes state EGAS). Rosneft (30%) does not appear anywhere in GEM's current Owner list, and 'Naturgy' / 'SEGAS' at 13% each have no sourced connection to the Zohr field or its pipelines at all: SEGAS is the SEPARATE operating company for the Damietta LNG plant (downstream of a different pipeline - the Al Gamil-Damietta line, GEM PID P6037), and Naturgy was historically a stakeholder in SEGAS/Damietta (via the former Eni-Naturgy 'Union Fenosa Gas' JV, pre-2021), never in Zohr field/pipeline equity. Checked against Wikipedia's SEGAS LNG page: current (post-Dec-2020 restructuring, closed Mar-2021) SEGAS shareholding is Eni 50% / EGAS 40% / EGPC 10% - no Naturgy, no 13% figures at all, under either the old or new SEGAS structure. The 48/26/13/13 split on this row does not match any known real ownership table for either entity, strongly suggesting a copy/misattribution error (most likely conflated with the Damietta LNG/SEGAS chain). Flagging per standing rule 3 (don't defend, verify) rather than auto-correcting; no owner change staged to the Owner tab pending human confirmation.

routes.start_name: Zohr field wellhead/manifold platforms, Shorouk concession, offshore Mediterranean Sea (Egypt EEZ)
routes.end_name: El-Gamil onshore gas treatment plant, Port Said Governorate, Egypt
routes.corridor_desc: Two parallel ~216 km, 30-inch subsea pipelines run from the Zohr field's wellhead/manifold platforms in the Shorouk concession (Mediterranean Sea, ~1,450-1,500 m water depth, sourced by NS Energy/Eni as ~190 km north of Port Said) roughly due south across the Egyptian EEZ continental slope and shelf to landfall at El-Gamil on the Port Said coast, terminating at the El-Gamil onshore gas treatment plant (8 production trains + sulphur units). No public subsea route trace or intermediate waypoints were found, so the corridor here is a straight-line bound between two independently sourced named endpoints, not a traced path. Sanity check: the great-circle distance between the sourced field coordinate (Wikidata, rounded to 33.0N/32.5E) and the El-Gamil/Port Said-airport coordinate (OurAirports, 31.2793N/32.2406E) computes to ~193 km - closely matching the independently reported ~190 km distance, which corroborates the general bearing/scale even though the exact endpoint coordinates are approximate (field position is a rounded Wikidata value; the onshore end uses the nearest well-documented 'El-Gamil' point, the former RAF/Port Said airport, as a proxy for the plant, which is in the same immediate locale but not confirmed to be the exact plant site).
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named, independently-sourced places (Zohr/Shorouk field per Wikidata; El-Gamil per NS Energy + OurAirports' airport entry as the best-documented point in that exact locale). No fabricated coordinates - field coordinate is Wikidata's own (rounded) value, not a GEM-derived figure; onshore point is a defensible nearby proxy, explicitly flagged as such rather than presented as the exact plant gate. No intermediate subsea waypoints could be sourced, so suggested_route_accuracy is capped at medium rather than high.
